technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot for rapid configuration and dependency injection.
Leverage Spring Batch for job and step execution.
Implement custom ItemReader and ItemWriter for JDBC and HDFS integration.
Use Spring Expression Language (SpEL) for dynamic directory/file naming.
Refactor MessageBus transformation logic to use a more efficient processing pipeline.
Integrate timeout handling using ScheduledExecutorService or Spring's @Scheduled with timeout control.
Use OpenCSV or Apache Commons CSV for CSV generation with delimiter escaping support.
assumptions: The project uses Java 17+ as required by Spring Framework 6.0.
Existing codebase already includes basic Spring Batch job configurations.
HDFS and JDBC connections are pre-configured and accessible.
Unit and integration testing frameworks (JUnit, Mockito) are already in place.
Developers are familiar with Spring ecosystem and Java concurrency patterns.
No external UI is required; all parameterization is done via configuration or command-line arguments.

activities.activity_description: Implement configuration options to dynamically generate code based on user input.
Allow users to configure merge behavior for incremental data consumption with Megastore.
Implement a configurable timeout mechanism to prevent jobs from running indefinitely.
Allow execution of SQL statements or scripts through job or processor components.
Allow users to inject custom RowMapper<Tuple> implementations to enrich JDBC data before writing to HDFS.
Enable use of expressions for dynamic naming of directories and files based on timestamps or other data points.
Implement delimiter escaping in CSV generation to ensure compatibility with Hive/HAWQ.
Refactor the MessageBus transformation logic to optimize throughput performance.
Write unit and integration tests for all new features and ensure compatibility with existing system.
